planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix; Marnier's Kalanchoe is drought-tolerant and rots quickly in wet or dense soil.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix. Marnier's Kalanchoe produces flattened, paddle-shaped, powdery blue-grey leaves arranged in neat opposite pairs along arching stems, each leaf edged in a fine pink-red margin that deepens with strong sun and cool weather, giving the whole plant a soft, two-toned pastel coloring. Clusters of pale pink to coral bell-shaped flowers dangle from the stem tips in winter to early spring, a welcome bloom period when many other succulents are dormant. Its arching, semi-trailing stems suit a raised bed, container edge, or hanging display. Water only when the soil has dried out completely, since it is prone to root and stem rot in constantly moist conditions.

planting.note: Grow in a hanging basket or elevated container in bright light in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix; Chandelier Plant blooms most heavily with a period of shorter days in fall to winter, similar to poinsettia.

directions: Grow in a hanging basket or elevated container in bright light in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix, watering only when the soil has dried out. Chandelier Plant, also called Copper Spoons, has small, rounded, spoon-shaped leaves along trailing stems that bear abundant clusters of dangling, bell-shaped, orange-red flowers in a heavy winter to early-spring bloom, transforming the whole plant into a hanging chandelier of color when few other succulents are flowering. Like poinsettia, it is a short-day bloomer, setting flower buds as days shorten in fall, so avoid exposing it to artificial light at night during that period if a heavy bloom is wanted. Its trailing habit and floriferous nature make it a favorite for hanging baskets and elevated displays rather than upright pots.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix, watering only when the soil has dried out completely. Pies from Heaven earns its whimsical name from its thick, diamond-shaped, fuzzy silvery-grey leaves marked with irregular brown-purple blotches near the tips, a distinctive mottled, felted texture unlike the smooth or waxy leaves of most other Madagascar kalanchoe species. Its slow-growing, sculptural, branching form and small scale make it a good collector's plant for a bright windowsill alongside other unusual dwarf succulents. Small pale yellow flowers may appear on mature plants but the mottled foliage is the main attraction. Avoid overwatering above all else, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot in the fuzzy, water-storing leaves.
